question_record.context: During the investigation of a potential ransomware activity on the device `vnevado-win11t`, several file system changes were discovered. The files included `get-userprttoken.ps1`, `characterical.zip`, and `characterical.zip.lockbit`. These changes, indicative of a ransomware attack, were linked back to activities of the Manatee Tempest group. This Russia-based cybercriminal group is known for deploying the Dridex banking trojan and collaborating with Mustard Tempest to gain network access. They use drive-by downloads, malvertising, and FakeUpdates to initiate attacks and then deploy Cobalt Strike for lateral movement and ransomware. More details can be found in the Actor Profile: Manatee Tempest Threat Analytics report.
question_record.question: What is the URL associated with the Manatee Tempest group's activity in this incident?
solution: Suspicious file system changes indicating possible ransomware activity have been observed, with a known malicious extension being appended to files. These activities were detected on an account with SID `S-1-5-21-1840191660-8534830288-125585561-1522`.

The threat actor group Manatee Tempest, known for deploying ransomware and using techniques such as malvertising and FakeUpdates infections, was observed. For more information about Manatee Tempest, please refer to the threat analytics report at `https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/a22c3410-db8f-4c58-866e-ebb760e509d0/analystreport`.

159.name: Possible ransomware activity based on a known malicious extension
159.description: Numerous file system changes have been observed on the device. The changes involve appending a file extension that is known and observed in past ransomware incidents. This file system activity might be indicative of mass encryption of files by ransomware.

135.name: Manatee Tempest activity group
135.description:
The actor that Microsoft tracks as Manatee Tempest is a Russia-based cybercriminal group that has been active since June 2014. It was notorious for one of its earliest malware lexpaigns – the Dridex banking trojan. Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. The actor also uses domain fronting to establish command-and-control channel for Cobalt Strike beacons. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

For more information, read the Actor Profile: Manatee Tempest Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/a22c3410-db8f-4c58-866e-ebb760e509d0/analystreport
